text: {"distance_m": 6, "reasoning_short": "This is an estimate from contrast-threshold data, not an exact figure. Acuity alone does not set the limit here: a 15% contrast spot drops below detection threshold before it reaches 1 arcmin. Under indoor lighting, lab data on small dark disks (Blackwell-type) put the threshold near 4% contrast at about 3.6 arcmin. For targets this small, threshold contrast rises roughly as 1/size² (Ricco-type summation). Scaling to 15% contrast gives a threshold size of about 1.9 arcmin, or 5.4e-4 rad. A 4 mm spot subtends that angle at about 7 m. Allowing a margin for reliable detection outside ideal lab conditions brings this to roughly 5–7 m, so about 6 m."}
